relations.subject: Nicholas Poppe
relations.evidence: He began teaching at the Institute for Modern Oriental Languages before he had completed his studies in 1920 at the age of 23.

relations.subject: Nicholas Poppe
relations.evidence: Three years later, in 1923, he began teaching at the University of Petrograd.

relations.role: head of the Department of Mongolian Studies
relations.evidence: In 1931, he was appointed head of the Department of Mongolian Studies in the Institute of Oriental Studies at the Soviet Academy of Sciences.

relations.subject: Nicholas Poppe
relations.evidence: Poppe joined the faculty of the Far East and Russian Institute at the University of Washington, where he taught until his retirement in 1968.

relations.subject: Nicholas Poppe
relations.evidence: In the 1950s, Poppe aided Senator Joseph McCarthy's campaign against Professor Owen Lattimore, whom McCarthy accused of being a Soviet agent. Poppe claimed during the 1952 hearings that Lattimore's work on Mongolia was "very superficial"
